slot.brief: Given a change in T and P for the same gas (or a comparison of two gases), find the new density or the ratio of densities using ρ = PM/RT; medium algebra but no unit traps.

stem: Two ideal gases A and B have equal densities when A is at pressure $2P$ and temperature $3T$, and B is at pressure $3P$ and temperature $2T$. What is $\dfrac{\rho_A}{\rho_B}$ when A is at pressure $3P$ and temperature $2T$, while B is at pressure $2P$ and temperature $3T$?

verdicts.working: For an ideal gas, ρ ∝ PM/T. The initial equality gives (2/3)M_A = (3/2)M_B, so M_A/M_B = 9/4. In the requested states, ρ_A/ρ_B = [(3/2)/(2/3)](M_A/M_B) = 81/16.

working:
Equal initial densities give $\dfrac{2M_A}{3T}=\dfrac{3M_B}{2T}$, so $\dfrac{M_A}{M_B}=\dfrac{9}{4}$. Hence, $\dfrac{\rho_A}{\rho_B}=\dfrac{M_A}{M_B}\dfrac{3/2}{2/3}=\dfrac{9}{4}\times\dfrac{9}{4}=\dfrac{81}{16}$.

Independent check: For an ideal gas, ρ ∝ PM/T. The initial equality gives (2/3)M_A = (3/2)M_B, so M_A/M_B = 9/4. In the requested states, ρ_A/ρ_B = [(3/2)/(2/3)](M_A/M_B) = 81/16.
solution:
For an ideal gas, $\rho\propto PM/T$. Equal initial densities give
$$\frac{2M_A}{3T}=\frac{3M_B}{2T}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\frac{M_A}{M_B}=\frac{9}{4}.$$
Thus, in the requested states, $\dfrac{\rho_A}{\rho_B}=\dfrac{M_A}{M_B}\dfrac{3/2}{2/3}=\dfrac{9}{4}\cdot\dfrac{9}{4}=\boxed{\dfrac{81}{16}}$.
